articles.title: Inside ‘Married at First Sight’ Season 20: How Peacock’s Changes Led to 1.8 Billion Minutes Viewed, That Wild Reunion and Why Lindsay Hubbard Said No to the Show
articles.summary: Millions of viewers are saying “I do” to Season 20 of “Married at First Sight.” The Kinetic Content relationship reality series, which moved to Peacock during Season 19 after 15 seasons on Lifetime, underwent a few changes this year.
body: Although the show aired on Peacock for Season 19, the 20th season is the first fully produced for Peacock, and it seems that the changes made really worked as it became a Top 3 reality title on streaming for five consecutive weeks, according to Nielsen.

“When we first acquired it, I was super excited — this is one of the great formats in unscripted history,” says Noah Samton, SVP of current production for Bravo and Peacock unscripted. “To have an opportunity to try to improve on what has already been established as something really strong, an opportunity to try to upgrade that and make it even better, is the most exciting challenge for me.”
Below, we dive more into those changes and upgrades with Samton — including the reunion that featured an audience for the first time.

Normally, if we acquired a show like this, I would try to watch every single episode. It just is impossible with this one. So I watched about 40 episodes, and it became very clear to me that there were some things that we could do to make it work better for a Peacock audience, make it a more fun, more exciting show, and just kind of revitalize it without losing what made it special and magical in the first place.

articles.summary: SPOILER ALERT: This article contains spoilers for “Big Little Truths,” the follow-up novel to “Big Little Lies.” It all starts with a mysterious finger sent to the school principal.
body: Additionally, Moriarty incorporates elements of “Big Little Lies” Season 2, like the introduction of Meryl Streep’s show-only character, Mary-Louise, into “Big Little Truths.”

In the sequel book, which hit shelves on Aug. 25, Moriarty picks up with Madeline (played by Reese Witherspoon on the HBO series), Jane (Shailene Woodley), Celeste (Nicole Kidman), Renata (Laura Dern) and Bonnie’s (Zoë Kravitz) lives as they experience a whirlwind of life changes following a 10-year time jump.

As their 15-year-old kids navigate the complicated emotions that come with being high-school students, the past also comes up like a current, leading the moms to reckon with what they haven’t told their kids about the circumstances under which Celeste’s husband, Perry (Alexander Skarsgård), was killed by Bonnie all those years ago.

Throughout “Big Little Truths,” Moriarty cuts back and forth between the moms’ perspectives and the months leading up to one big event: “D-Day,” which is revealed to be the infamous day on which Jane’s son Ziggy and his classmates give a presentation that reveals the true intentions of their new red-haired history teacher, Melody.

articles.title: Marketing meltdown: why has Andrew Garfield’s new film suddenly added Robin Hood?
articles.summary: Paul Greengrass drama The Uprising was supposed to be a historical epic about the Peasants’ Revolt of 1381 – but a strange new campaign has inserted a surprising figure. Nobody likes to have the full plot of a movie spoiled before they’ve even seen it.
body: Here’s what we know so far. Initially, all the trailers and promotional materials made The Uprising look like a film about the Peasants’ Revolt that tore through England in 1381. And this was very exciting, since the revolt was a thrilling moment in history that has been bizarrely underserved by Hollywood over the years. Most exciting of all, though, it sounded like it fit exactly into Greengrass’s wheelhouse: full of action and realism and political awareness.

But that all changed this week, when the film’s US distributor, Focus Features, announced the film’s full title on social media. What had once simply been The Uprising was now The Uprising: The Rise of Robin Hood. It added a new synopsis, reading: “Set against the true events of the Uprising that helped inspire the legend of Robin Hood, [Andrew Garfield’s character] forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice.”

articles.title: What we know after the big Grand Theft Auto 6 preview
articles.summary: The official look at the blockbuster video game leaves fans and critics impressed.
body: After more than 18 months since the last official glimpse of Grand Theft Auto 6, developer Rockstar has shown fans a 26-minute preview of the upcoming blockbuster video game.
Its "extended look" debuted on Netflix, six hours before going live on YouTube, and was the first chance players have had to see detailed footage of the title in action.
The montage, with no commentary or explanatory captions, showed off improved graphics, detailed environments and a selection of car-chases and shoot-outs from the sequel.
The broadcast followed a week of unauthorised gameplay leaks, which the developer said it had been "heartbreaking" to see shared online.
points: The official look at the blockbuster video game leaves fans and critics impressed.

articles.summary: Hamish Linklater and Owen Teague also star in James Ashcroft’s film of Alex North’s crime novel about a series of abductions of young boys in smalltown New Jersey.
body: Around the same time, widowed crime writer Tom Kennedy ( Adam Scott ) relocates from the Jersey shore to the small town where he and his late wife grew up, hoping the change of environment will benefit his traumatized eight-year-old son Jake (Acston Luca Porto). But Jake seems ill at ease in the spacious old home his dad rented (sharp work from production designer Anastasia White), seeking comfort in the presence of an imaginary friend he brought along in the move.

Meanwhile, Det. Beck finds eerie similarities between the recently discovered corpse and those of victims in a trail of killings from some 25 years earlier, committed by a murderer who became known as the Whisper Man for the way he beckoned his prey through their windows at night. The creepy nursery rhyme associated with those crimes has lingered in gruesome local folklore. But the culprit, Frank Carter — Netflix has requested that reviews not reveal the name of the unbilled actor playing him — remains behind bars, serving a life sentence.

articles.title: Inside the Halloween Horror Nights ‘Stranger Things’ House and Epic Effort to Bring the Duffer Brothers’ World to Life
articles.summary: Creatives from Universal Studios Hollywood and Universal Orlando Resort take The Hollywood Reporter inside their final house and first-ever lagoon show.
body: When Universal Studios Hollywood debuted its Stranger Things house as part of the bicoastal Halloween Horror Nights 2018 event, it was already two years into the show’s pop-culture takeover. Season one had garnered buzz, but the Duffer Brothers -created series would ultimately cement itself — and its ensemble of young stars — into a massive global hit by season two, just in time for its HHN debut.

Now, nearly a year after the Netflix show’s long-awaited conclusion and during the 10-year an n iversary of its series debut, Murdy confirms the cast has already been asked back to take a final walk through Hawkins and the Upside Down — alongside their fans. Opening on Sept. 3 in Hollywood and Aug. 28 in Orlando, the Stranger Things 5 houses will double as the end of an era for Netflix and as a major milestone for the after-hours event, which will have adapted the entirety of a TV series for one of the first times in its history.

articles.title: This Classic Haunted House Novel That Stephen King Declared The Scariest Ever Needs A Faithful Adaptation
articles.summary: Stephen King praised this 1970s horror story as the 'scariest haunted house house novel ever written,' but it's still in need of a faithful movie adaptation.
body: On one hand, Richard Matheson's "Hell House" was published at precisely the right time. It hit shelves the same year Ken Russell's "The Devils" scandalized moviegoers, but wasn't as aggressively sacrilegious in its portrayal of orgiastic behavior. Given how hard horror was going, and how much harder it was about to go, at that moment (via "The Last House on the Left," "The Exorcist" and "The Texas Chainsaw Massacre"), a faithful adaptation of Matheson's novel would've been shredding the outside of the same sordid envelope.

The decision was made to mostly allude to the hardcore sexual elements of the novel, which left us with John Hough's creepy "The Legend of Hell House" in 1974 (though rated PG at the time, it would no doubt receive an R today, if only for its adult material and intense scares). It's a spooky movie, but it doesn't quite measure up to Stephen King's declaration that "'Hell House' is the scariest haunted house novel ever written. It looms over the rest the way a mountain looms over foothills."
points: Stephen King praised this 1970s horror story as the 'scariest haunted house house novel ever written,' but it's still in need of a faithful movie adaptation.

articles.title: Robert Carlyle: ‘When we did The Full Monty strip, the reaction from the crowd was terrifying’
articles.summary: The actor on which star he’d devour first on a lifeboat, why he prefers pigeons to dogs and how Trainspotting put the Scottish accent on the map. You’re stranded on a lifeboat with Ewan McGregor, Ewen Bremner, Jonny Lee Miller, Kevin McKidd, Peter Mullan, James Cosmo, Keith Allen and Irvine Welsh.
body: I’m sure this will disappoint people, but there must have been 10 Wee Jocks. I just don’t like working with animals because they don’t know they’re acting, so it can take them 10 takes to cross a road. The best animals I’ve ever worked with were the pigeons on The Full Monty TV show, which we had to chase. I thought: “This is never going to work.” But they just did what they were told and would fly out of their box and land on your shoulder. I love pigeons now. Dogs, not so much.

What was it like to look in the mirror and see John Lennon staring back at you in Yesterday? MegMay I don’t particularly look like John Lennon, but apparently there’s something about the bridge of my nose that looks a bit like his, which is what the wonderful prosthetics people focused on. When they were putting it all on, I’d sunk quite low in the chair, so I could only see the top of my head in the mirror. When they finished and I sat up, it was quite freaky.

articles.title: Golf Channel Cancels ‘Big Break x Good Good’ After PGA Tour Parts Ways With YouTube Stars
articles.summary: With no Good Good Championship following one bad bad commercial, the 2026 'Big Break' winner loses his sponsorship exemption into the tournament.
body: Golf Channel has canceled its fully filmed 2026 season of Big Break, the Versant-owned cable network’s signature reality competition series. It sort of had no choice — or at least no ultimate purpose for airing the season as planned.

“Following recent developments involving Good Good, and including the fact that the intended outcome of the series can no longer be fulfilled, Golf Channel will not be able to complete this season of Big Break as planned,” Golf Channel said in a statement. “While we are disappointed for the 12 competitors, our production team that worked tirelessly on the season, and the show’s passionate fans, we look forward to Big Break ’s return to Golf Channel in 2027.”
Big Break aired on Golf Channel from 2003-2015. This was set to be its big comeback.
